headline: Infrastructure platform consolidating materials, products, and logistics into a capital-compounding control point
standout_number: $8.5B Arcosa acquisition commitment + 12th consecutive year of margin expansion (20.5% EBITDA margin in 2025)
whats_different: CRH monetizes not just cement demand but the connected ecosystem of materials, roads, water infrastructure, and building solutions. The company is moving beyond commodity cyclicality into platform-style capital allocation and recurring infrastructure intensity driven by data-center demand, electrification, and aging utility networks.
watch: Water infrastructure (Axius Water) penetration into municipal and utility networks; execution on Arcosa integration; ability to maintain pricing discipline through margin expansion in non-residential categories while residential remains soft.

headline: Housing cost structure play executing portfolio modernization through a downcycle to emerge with lower-cost, high-quality footprint
standout_number: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of only $56M (1% margin) through restructuring and impairment charges of $712M; Q2 2026 showed rebound with Henderson starting, producing positive EBITDA
whats_different: West Fraser is readable as a cycle recovery and modernization story rather than just lumber weakness. The company explicitly chose 2025 to close undereconomic mills, start high-efficiency Henderson, and reposition the geographic mix toward the US South. This shows capital discipline during trough rather than just survival mode.
watch: Henderson ramp-up trajectory and whether improved cost structure holds as prices normalize; US-South mill utilization and pricing power; whether tariff environment remains supportive for US-based production.

headline: Nuclear fuel cycle control system capturing contract-backed long-term uranium demand and Westinghouse equity upside
standout_number: Long-term commitments to deliver ~230M pounds of uranium at ~28M pounds annually over next 5 years; Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA $391M down from Q2 2025 $352M due to lower equity earnings from Westinghouse and delivery timing, not uranium weakness
whats_different: Cameco is not a pure uranium-price play. It monetizes the entire fuel cycle through mining, procurement, inventory management, conversion, long-term contracting, and a strategic stake in Westinghouse. The company's margins depend on contract visibility and reactor deployment as much as spot uranium prices.
watch: Westinghouse profitability and global reactor construction pipeline (Dukovany mentioned); Q1 2026 showed uranium segment driving improvement through higher realized prices; whether contracted uranium base continues to rise as energy security justifies more reactor capex.

headline: Workforce-shortage arbitrage converting healthcare labor scarcity into scaled institutional training throughput
standout_number: FY2026 Q4 total enrollment 99,472 up 8.4% YoY; full-year revenue ~$1.95B with adjusted EPS ~$8.25; healthcare educator positioned as 'America's largest healthcare educator' tied to nursing, physician, veterinary shortages
whats_different: Adtalem/Covista reframes education as labor-market infrastructure rather than discretionary prestige or general learning. The company's growth engine is institutional shortage (healthcare), employer partnerships, and credential value alignment with actual hiring need. This is education sold as infrastructure capacity rather than lifestyle aspiration.
watch: Enrollment retention and outcome tracking (job readiness metrics); employer collaboration deepening; whether AI-oriented credentials (mentioned in Q2 results) can expand addressable market; regulatory scrutiny on workforce training quality and access.

headline: Multi-format staples packaging platform where dispensing closures and specialty components carry higher value than commodity food cans
standout_number: Dispensing and Specialty Closures segment produced $2.7B revenue and $321.5M EBITDA in 2025 (~50% of total EBITDA) while Metal Containers and Custom Containers compete on scale
whats_different: Silgan monetizes the hidden layer between raw materials and consumer goods through four operating channels: closures for fragrance/beauty (high-value), metal food containers (scale), custom containers (diversified), and specialty components. Raw-material pass-through masks the real story: Silgan wins through closure design, customer tooling relationships, and portfolio diversity, not just throughput.
watch: Fragrance and beauty dispensing momentum (double-digit growth in Q1 2026); pet-food metal container attach rates; whether raw-material cost pass-through remains complete; custom container profitability trend.

headline: Comfort-driven mass cultural shift monetized through brand ubiquity, international growth, and majority direct-to-consumer channel
standout_number: Q2 2026 Crocs Brand revenue surpassed $1.0B quarterly for first time; 59% of FY2025 revenue through DTC (direct) channels; full-year FY2025 revenue ~$4.04B across 85+ countries
whats_different: Crocs is not a niche product. It is mass casualization normalized. The company's real advantage is that comfort has become culturally accepted across age groups and occasions, enabling global scale, high direct margins, and pricing power. HEYDUDE remains a repair project, but core Crocs brand is cultural lockdown, not product novelty.
watch: DTC channel sustenance and pricing (currently at 59%+ mix); international growth rates (double-digit through 2026); whether comfort casualization continues or faces saturation; HEYDUDE stabilization.

headline: Free-cash-flow maximization and shareholder yield model with 193% reserve replacement and disciplined Delaware Basin concentration
standout_number: Q2 2026 (first full post-Coterra quarter) adjusted free cash flow $1.7B; standalone Q1 2026 FCF $816M on production of 833K BOe/d; production costs $10.99/BOe in Q4 2025 with 193% reserve replacement
whats_different: Devon is not a production-growth story. It is a capital-discipline and shareholder-return story. The company prioritizes Delaware Basin quality, free cash flow conversion, and fixed dividend plus buyback policy over production maximization. Post-merger scale changes this, but the underlying discipline remains focused.
watch: Coterra integration success and combined Delaware Basin position; whether merger-enabled $5B+ buyback authorization gets deployed; Waha pricing and midstream infrastructure constraints; whether free cash flow margins hold as production scales.

headline: LNG export chokepoint capturing scarce liquefaction capacity value through customer-backed expansion and long-contract visibility
standout_number: Q2 2026 record 184 LNG cargoes exported in quarter with Distributable Cash Flow $1.2B; Corpus Christi Stage 3 Midscale Trains 1-6 completed/operational with Train 7 imminent; raised FY2026 guidance to $7.90B-$8.40B Adjusted EBITDA
whats_different: Cheniere monetizes infrastructure scarcity and customer lock-in, not commodity prices. The company is expanding liquefaction capacity with explicit customer support (Meta agreement), operates on long-term contracts, and generates distributions that are capital-return-focused. This is infrastructure toll economics wrapped in energy packaging.
watch: Blackwell train completion and ramp-up (Trains 5-7 in 2026); continuation of customer-backed expansion agreements beyond Meta; any LNG pricing power shift; whether high utilization and record cargos can be sustained.

headline: Merchant refiner snapback recovery on Martinez restart combined with cost improvement and debt reduction, but with higher leverage and event risk exposure
standout_number: Q2 2026 income from operations $1.272B vs excluding special items $1.054B; Q2 gross margin $14.20/barrel; received $250M fifth insurance installment related to Martinez fire; debt reduced by >$1B in quarter; Martinez returned to full operations in Q2
whats_different: PBF is a turnaround case in recovery mode. The Martinez fire in Feb 2025 was a real event; recovery happened faster than feared. The company's earnings power depends on operational execution, insurance cash, and whether a good cycle is used to strengthen or just to restore optionality. This is higher-risk but higher-potential-upside than pure downstream leaders.
watch: Martinez full ramp and operational stability; whether crack spreads and coastal refining premiums justify the event risk; debt reduction pace and leverage trajectory; renewable diesel (St. Bernard) production ramp to 18K-20K BOe/d.

headline: Permanent capital allocation machine using insurance float, diversified operating cash, and retained earnings to compound across unlike businesses
standout_number: FY2025 net earnings $66.968B; operating earnings $44.486B; repurchased $4.5B treasury shares in Q2 2026 and $4.8B in first half 2026
whats_different: Berkshire is not valued for one segment or one moat. It is valued for capital allocation skill, patience, and the ability to sit above operating units with permanent capital. Insurance, BNSF, BHE, manufacturing, and retail can be weak individually but collectively create optionality that markets underprice.
watch: Operating earnings composition and which segments are supporting the cash generation; continued capital return cadence and whether large cash balance remains for opportunistic deployment; succession clarity and cultural continuation.

headline: Specialty underwriting discipline plus long-horizon investing model competing against brokers through decentralized operating portfolio and capital allocation
standout_number: 2025 operating income $3.2B; adjusted operating income >$2.3B; insurance adjusted operating income rose 16%; combined ratio improved to 95%
whats_different: Markel is not a pure insurance play and not a pure capital allocator. It is a hybrid that compounds through specialty underwriting skill, investment discipline, and a diversified collection of operating businesses. This makes it less scale-dependent than brokers and more underwriting-focused than pure balance-sheet players.
watch: Specialty underwriting profit momentum and combined ratio trend; investment portfolio performance given rate environment; operating company integration and whether the diversified portfolio creates competitive advantage or complexity.

headline: Generics-to-branded transition where scale hedges commodity pressure while innovative portfolio capture enables margin escape
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue ~$4.1B with innovative brands raising outlook to combined 2026 revenue ~$3.7B; generics still provide scale and reach but branded growth (AUSTEDO, etc.) increasingly determines performance
whats_different: Teva is readable as a portfolio-mix story more than a pure scale or innovation story. Generics remain large but commoditized; branded pipeline (neuroscience, immunology) carries better margins. The company is transitioning from manufacturing efficiency-dependent to mix-dependent earnings, requiring execution and capital discipline rather than just volume.
watch: Innovative brand contribution and whether branded growth reaches projected $3.7B for FY2026; lenalidomide revenue decline management; transformation cost realization; biosimilar competitive positions.

headline: Recurring healthcare middle layer combining diagnostics, devices, nutrition, and pharma into embedded workflow and installed-base system
standout_number: 2025 revenue $44.328B; Medical Devices $19.290B, Diagnostics $9.888B, Nutritional $8.820B, Established Pharma $6.330B; Q2 2026 Diagnostics growth >12% with Exact Sciences March 2026 close expanding reach
whats_different: Abbott monetizes repeated use, testing, and monitoring rather than one-time procedures or acute interventions. The diagnostics-devices-nutrition portfolio creates multiple touch points with hospitals, labs, patients, and providers. This is workflow embeddedness through product breadth and recurring consumables rather than single-device dominance.
watch: Exact Sciences integration and synergy realization; chronic-disease demand (diabetes, cardiovascular) sustainability; nutrition category performance in developed vs emerging markets; diagnostic throughput growth post-integration.

headline: Aging-in-place labor-intensive recurring care platform consolidating regional fragmentation into scaled local density
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue $377.4M; personal care 78.4% of revenue, hospice 17.0%, home health 4.6%; adjusted EBITDA $49.2M; record annual revenue of $1.42B in FY2025 with 5th consecutive year of double-digit growth
whats_different: Addus does not sell clinical acuity or innovation. It sells lower-cost care continuity, caregiver density, state rate support, and acquisition-built local scale. The company monetizes the economic truth that keeping people at home is cheaper than institutional care and that fragmented markets consolidate toward scaled operators with compliance systems.
watch: State rate increases (Texas and Illinois mentioned) and reimbursement environment; caregiver wage pressure and retention; acquisition integration success; whether profitability can grow alongside scale or whether labor inflation caps margins.

headline: Physical infrastructure components platform where utility poles, coatings, telecom hardware, and irrigation sit inside grid modernization and electrification demand
standout_number: Q2 2026 guidance raised to $4.3B-$4.45B sales (from $4.2B-$4.4B) and $22.25-$23.50 diluted EPS; North America Utility sales grew 21%; backlog increased to $1.65B with utility driving primarily; Section 232 tariff uncertainty on steel poles
whats_different: Valmont is misread as a generic conglomerate. It is actually a coherent physical-layer portfolio: utility poles, structures, coatings, telecom hardware, and irrigation drive by grid expansion, data-center density, and farm productivity. The key is that AI and electrification first show up as utility pole and coatings demand before appearing as application-level monetization.
watch: North America Utility backlog conversion and whether 21% growth rate sustains; tariff impact on Mexican-sourced poles; agriculture downcycle recovery timing; carrier spending weakness containment in Telecommunications segment.

headline: Field-execution layer monetizing telecom fiber, data-center power, wireless, and underground utility work tied to AI infrastructure deployment
standout_number: Fiscal Q1 2027 (May 2026) record contract revenues $1.965B (+46.5% YoY backlog); total backlog record $11.906B (2.2x book-to-bill); book-to-bill reached 2.2x on fiber, data-center, and BEAD demand
whats_different: Dycom is not generic heavy construction. It monetizes the field-execution, labor, and routing work required to deploy digital infrastructure. AI and fiber demand translate into planning, engineering, aerial construction, wireless work, and inside-plant cabling. Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators acquisitions extend the company upstream into data-center electrical systems.
watch: BEAD broadband subsidy deployment and state-level approval pace; fiber-to-the-home program acceleration; data-center buildout sustainability and pricing; Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators integration success; customer duration extensions and labor retention.

headline: Institutional execution infrastructure monetizing federal complexity, energy transition, and disaster/resilience administration through outcome-based contracts
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue $474.5M (nearly flat YoY); federal revenue down 9.5% YoY; commercial revenue up 5.9%; pipeline up 9% sequentially to $9.3B; technology modernization alone represented ~50% of Q2 federal revenue and ~$2.6B of pipeline
whats_different: ICF is not consulting in the traditional sense. It is execution infrastructure for institutions that are operationally stressed and require outside help with modernization, energy programs, grants, compliance, disaster recovery, and resilience planning. Federal noise does not eliminate need; it reroutes demand toward fixed-price and outcome-based work.
watch: Commercial energy services growth and market share (35% in residential, approaching 20% in C&I); technology modernization pipeline conversion; federal procurement normalization; international growth acceleration.

headline: Regional route density platform with landfill control and recycling-solutions breadth creating integrated waste and resource management in Northeast/Mid-Atlantic
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue $543.7M; solid waste pricing up 5.5% (collection +5.8%, disposal +4.7%); adjusted EBITDA $123.2M; five acquisitions closed YTD 2026 with ~$165M annualized revenue
whats_different: Casella is regionally concentrated and not trying to be national scale. It monetizes local route density, landfill ownership, recycling systems, and acquisition-driven consolidation in fragmented Northeast/Mid-Atlantic markets. This is density and local execution advantage rather than national logistics scale.
watch: Mid-Atlantic integration success and systems consolidation progress; recycling commodity price exposure and whether Resource Solutions margins hold; acquisition pipeline continuation; PFAS and environmental remediation cost pressures.

headline: Housing-finance carry vehicle capturing mortgage servicing spreads and agency liquidity value through leverage, hedging, and dividend defense
standout_number: 2025 aggregate economic return 20.2% including 5.5% book-value gain; Q2 2026 economic return 5.5%; dividend increased to $0.75/share; economic leverage ~5.6x; portfolio ~$109.4B
whats_different: Annaly is valuable when rate conditions and portfolio construction cooperate. It captures housing-finance exposure without owning credit risk, but does depend on repo funding, hedge effectiveness, and rate environment stability. The moat is much more fragile than deposit or fee franchises.
watch: Book-value stability through rate cycles; dividend sustainability as interest-rate regime clarifies; repo funding availability; whether positive economic returns persist through normalization.

headline: IPG-merged attention infrastructure combining media, data, identity, and AI tooling to coordinate fragmented client budgets across channels
standout_number: Q2 2026 core revenue $6.0B (6.1% organic growth); non-GAAP adjusted EBITA $1.1B (17.8% core margin); IPG merger closed Nov 2025; management tied demand to agentic marketing, connected commerce, and AI-driven discovery
whats_different: Omnicom is not creative-house or media-buying simplicity. It is a control layer that helps clients navigate fragmented media, identity, targeting, and measurement at scale. The merger with IPG creates platform scale and data density that smaller or narrower agencies cannot match.
watch: IPG integration execution and cost synergy realization; organic growth sustainability amid client budget uncertainty; AI and automation adoption pace by major clients; talent retention post-merger.

headline: Route-based workplace-services compounder with 95% of revenue from recurring customer location servicing and pricing power
standout_number: FY2026 Q4 revenue $2.91B; operating margin 23.1%; FY2026 full-year revenue $10.340B, net income $1.812B, diluted EPS $4.40; FY2027 guidance $12.10B-$12.25B revenue
whats_different: Cintas is not apparel retail. It is outsourced workplace services (uniforms, facility services, first aid, safety, fire protection) monetized through route density and customer location density. The model produces pricing power, retention, cross-sell, and strong free cash flow because switching costs are high once installed.
watch: UniFirst acquisition completion and integration (FTC second request expected); margin sustainability at scale; cross-sell penetration into customer base; labor cost management and field productivity.

headline: Premium lifestyle home retailer executing brand discipline and operating leverage despite tariff pressure through multi-brand portfolio (Pottery Barn, West Elm, Rejuvenation)
standout_number: FY2025 (ended Feb 2026) comparable brand revenue +3.5%; operating margin 18.1%; diluted EPS $8.84 (record); FY2026 Q1 comparable revenue +4.8%, operating margin 16.2%; ~$60M incremental tariff costs embedded
whats_different: Williams-Sonoma monetizes home as lifestyle, hosting, and occasion consumption rather than just furniture replacement. Multi-brand architecture (cooking, dining, kids, gifting, outdoor) creates occasions and customer stickiness. Tariffs are real but managed through supply-chain discipline and margin protection.
watch: Tariff impact trajectory through 2026 (front-loaded in H1); DTC and omnichannel execution; design-services and B2B growth; inventory management amid tariff timing pull-forward; whether premium margins can sustain.

headline: Children's reading and school-channel distribution monetizing franchise IP through Book Fairs, book clubs, retail, digital platforms, and animated production
standout_number: FY2026 full-year revenue ~$1.582B; adjusted EBITDA up 4% to ~$151.5M; Book Fairs revenue in Q4 up 5% to $186.6M; Entertainment revenue up 42% in Q4 to $21.0M; streaming app launched with 3.5M+ views
whats_different: Scholastic owns children's attention through trusted institutional access (schools, educators, Book Fairs) and beloved franchises rather than through mass digital platforms. The company monetizes reading habits, family consumption, school events, and entertainment extensions at once. Sale-leaseback and buyback noise masks underlying franchise strength.
watch: Book Fairs and trade strength sustaining amid school budget pressure; Entertainment platform scaling (streaming, YouTube, animated series production); Education Solutions recovery; free cash flow being deployed into shareholder returns vs growth reinvestment.

headline: Foodservice distribution intermediary capturing institutional meal-system economics through route density, customer mix, and procurement efficiency
standout_number: FY2025 net sales $39.4B (+4.1%); adjusted EBITDA $1.93B (11.0% growth); Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA $604M (record); independent restaurant case volume +5.1%, healthcare +3.5%, hospitality +4.4%
whats_different: US Foods monetizes the middle layer between producers and consumers through foodservice operators (restaurants, hospitals, hotels, schools). The moat is route density, customer segmentation, private-label growth, and digital ordering (MOXe platform) that embeds the distributor into customer workflows.
watch: Independent restaurant volume growth sustainability amid consumer caution; healthcare and hospitality segment dynamics; private-label penetration and margin capture; MOXe platform adoption and unit economics.

headline: Search and observability platform monetizing enterprise AI context layer through unstructured-data retrieval, vector search, and security analytics
standout_number: Fiscal Q3 2026 (ended May 2026) revenue $449.9M (18% YoY growth); subscription revenue $426M; remaining performance obligations $1.982B; cash/equivalents $768.7M; management branded Elastic as 'Search AI Company'
whats_different: Elastic sits at the enterprise AI context bottleneck. The company does not own infrastructure or application workflows, but rather the software layer that makes fragmented enterprise logs, telemetry, and unstructured data usable for search, observability, security, and AI retrieval. This is a hidden toll collector in the infrastructure stack.
watch: Subscription revenue growth pace and cloud adoption acceleration; remaining performance obligations conversion; whether gross margins can expand as software mix matures; customer AI use-case adoption.

headline: Optical and materials science platform capturing AI data-center density and infrastructure intensity through fiber, glass, and manufacturing partnerships
standout_number: Q2 2026 Optical Communications sales grew 32% to $2.07B; Enterprise Networks up 65%; core operating margin 20.9%; management tied momentum to Amazon and NVIDIA partnerships; multiyear customer commitments including Meta
whats_different: Corning is a physical-layer toll collector hidden in the technology taxonomy. The company monetizes optical fiber density, advanced materials, and manufacturing credibility to support AI data centers, telecom builds, and connected devices. This is not software governance but rather the physical transmission medium that must exist before any control layer matters.
watch: Optical Communications growth sustainability and whether hyperscale CapEx pullback could moderate growth; customer-backed capacity expansion execution; margins and ROIC trajectory (targeting 14-15% range); solar and advanced materials contributions.

headline: Wholesale optical transport and on-net IP backbone monetizing AI and cloud traffic movement between enterprises, carriers, and data centers
standout_number: FY2025 service revenue $975.8M with adjusted EBITDA margin 31.9%; Q2 2026 IP traffic growth 16% YoY with on-net revenue $150.2M; wavelength revenue growing; data-center sale for $224.2M with $130.7M gain
whats_different: Cogent monetizes the middle of the stack: transport and peering between enterprise sites, content networks, carriers, and cloud. The company is not a consumer access play and not a raw hardware supplier. It is value concentrated in route placement, on-net density, and wavelength attachment where data-movement demand is highest.
watch: On-net revenue share growth and whether wavelength uptake continues; off-net contraction management; acquisition of owned data centers and whether monetization via sale-leasebacks proves repeatable; leverage reduction trajectory.

headline: Mission-software and national-security modernization platform monetizing government funding through electronic warfare, geospatial intelligence, and Agile modernization
standout_number: Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue $2.71B (+17.6% YoY); annual revenue $9.6B with EBITDA margin 12.3%; total backlog $32.0B (1.1x book-to-bill); contract awards $10.2B; ARKA acquisition ($2.1B) expands space and sensing
whats_different: CACI is not generic federal IT services. It monetizes mission-critical modernization, electronic warfare, geospatial intelligence, Agile software delivery, and space-based sensing for national-security customers. This is government dependence that produces recurring demand due to strategic necessity rather than budget availability.
watch: ARKA acquisition integration and whether space/geospatial expansion drives higher margins; funded backlog growth and whether near-term revenue visibility improves; electronic warfare and counter-drone market adoption; continued AI/ML investment in mission systems.

headline: Local-commerce marketplace and logistics infrastructure coordinating consumer convenience behavior, merchant density, and delivery networks
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue $4.454B (36% YoY growth); Marketplace GOV $33.1B (36% growth); orders 970M (+27% YoY); DashPass membership >35M across brands; adjusted EBITDA $914M (+40% YoY)
whats_different: DoorDash is misclassified as internet access. It is a local-commerce coordination platform that monetizes recurring convenience behavior, merchant aggregation, membership, and logistics density. The company's real asset is the coordination layer between consumers, merchants, and couriers, not direct retail or delivery alone.
watch: Marketplace GOV growth sustainability and whether orders can re-accelerate; membership growth and penetration (DashPass, Wolt+, Deliveroo Plus); international expansion (Deliveroo, Wolt); advertising and merchant-tools monetization.

headline: Stressed communications-infrastructure vendor facing component supply constraints and carrier CapEx weakness after strategic divestitures
standout_number: FY2025 net sales $1.93B; Q2 2026 net sales $319.6M with Core adjusted EBITDA $45.5M; CCS sale proceeds used to repay all debt and redeem preferred equity; distributions $10.00 per share in April 2026, $5.00 announced for August
whats_different: CommScope/Vistance shows the stress case where bandwidth demand does not guarantee value capture. Divestitures of high-value assets (CCS), component pricing pressure, and narrower residual Aurora platform make this a capital-return and wind-down story rather than a growth trajectory.
watch: Aurora platform profitability and whether memory-chip pricing/availability normalizes; stranded costs from divestitures and whether operating efficiency can recover; remaining optical and infrastructure opportunities; whether capital distribution pace is sustainable.

headline: Full-stack AI infrastructure platform capturing value across chips, systems, networking, software, and reference designs driving datacenter-as-factory buildout
standout_number: FY2027 Q1 revenue $81.6B; Data Center revenue $75.2B (91% of total); operating income $53.5B; record $20.2B buybacks in Q1 with additional $80B authorization; China Data Center revenue not in outlook
whats_different: NVIDIA is not a chip vendor alone. It monetizes full-stack infrastructure where H100/H200 chips are just one layer. Blackwell systems, NVLink networking, CUDA software, and reference designs for hyperscalers create platform lock-in and margin defense. The company captures value across the entire AI infrastructure stack.
watch: Blackwell ramp across hyperscalers, model builders, sovereigns; whether Gaming supply constraints persist; Rubin architecture adoption and demand; leverage and export policy exposure; whether datacenter margins compress as competition intensifies.

headline: Large regulated transmission-and-distribution utility platform generating durable earnings through rate base growth and infrastructure modernization
standout_number: Q2 2026 adjusted operating earnings $0.43/share; FY2026 guidance $2.81-$2.91/share; revised $41.7B four-year capital plan with 7.9% expected rate-base growth; additional $12B-$17B transmission opportunity identified
whats_different: Exelon is not a generation or data-center demand play. It is a regulated wires platform with top-quartile reliability performance (ComEd in top decile). The company generates earnings through approved rate recovery, distribution modernization, and transmission expansion visibility rather than through headline load growth announcements.
watch: Rate-base recovery mechanisms and whether 90% coverage through 2026-2027 holds; transmission opportunity monetization beyond base capital plan; reliability performance maintenance; regulated vs unregulated mix evolution post-Constellation separation.
